subject: Provisional capacity queueing + conditional hold for PolarisML ramp
messages:
From: Gavin Suri <gavin.suri@polarisml.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@polarisml.ai
Date: 2026-12-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PolarisML - capacity query and provisional hold request

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. PolarisML is moving into final commercial discussions and we have a Q1 ramp that will require a dedicated slice of GPUs for inference and fine-tuning work. Before we roll procurement internally we need to understand short-term availability and whether Redwood can place a provisional hold while we finalize the SOW.

Ballpark ask: 120 A100-equivalent GPUs (or compatible quantized variants) across a dedicated pool, starting mid-Jan, with the ability to scale +40% in the first 60 days. We know this is sizeable — if a full reservation isn't possible immediately we'd like a soft 30-day hold that prevents capacity from being reallocated, plus an ops-level contact for staging/canary runs.

I've attached a high-level SLA/requirements doc (polaris_sla_request.pdf). Can you confirm next steps and what information you need from us to lock a provisional hold?

Appreciate it —
Gavin
Gavin Suri
Head of Infrastructure, PolarisML
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Gavin Suri <gavin.suri@polarisml.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-03T11:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisML - capacity query and provisional hold request

Gavin — thanks, and congrats on making it to the finish line.

Short answers up front: we can offer a conditional 30-day soft hold on the requested capacity and a staged scaling plan provided Polaris signs the provisional hold form and confirms the baseline commit by the hold expiration. To proceed we need:
- final anticipated sustained concurrency (tokens/sec or QPS) and target sequence lengths for your main inference workloads
- expected percent of training/fine-tune vs inference (ops mix affects node packing)
- confirmation of tolerance for quantized variants (we can often meet A100-equivalent throughput with int8/4-bit profiles)

I've attached our provisional_hold_form.docx — sign+return and we'll seed a soft hold within 24 hours. Internal ops will run a capacity snapshot and return a recommended allocation. If you can get procurement to agree to the DocuSign link and a 30-day decision window, we can start staging nodes for canary testing.

Next steps:
1) Polaris returns signed provisional form (attached)
2) Redwood ops runs a resource mapping and publishes a capacity snapshot (I expect this by EOD 12/04)
3) Exchange of canary test plan and schedule

Looping Ben and Karthik on ops and capacity.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-04T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisML - capacity query and provisional hold request (internal)

Chloe / Karthik — quick ops check from inventory and scheduler POV:

Current fleet (US regions):
- Free A100-eq slots across Dedicated pools: ~96 GPUs (after existing soft commitments)
- Idle spot/ephemeral capacity that can be converted quickly: ~48 GPUs (with ~24h prep)
- Quantized profile expected uplift: ~+30% effective capacity if Polaris accepts int8/4-bit (depends on model architecture)

Recommendation: we can seed a soft hold for 120 A100-equivalent by mixing 80 dedicated + 40 convertible ephemeral nodes, with a plan to convert an additional 20 ephemeral nodes to dedicated within 10 business days of firm commit. Key caveats:
- We need firmization within the 30-day hold window; otherwise ephemeral nodes will be re-allocated.
- If Polaris insists on strict A100 hardware (no quantization), we can only guarantee ~85% of the requested capacity without rebalancing other late-stage deals.

I'll prepare the capacity_snapshot_20261204.csv and include node-level IDs. Karthik — can you review the proposed conversion schedule and confirm the ops SLA for canary testing (we typically guarantee a 48h staging window once nodes are reserved)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Gavin Suri <gavin.suri@polarisml.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@polarisml.ai
Date: 2026-12-05T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisML - capacity query and provisional hold request

Gavin — following up with the ops summary and next steps.

Attached: provisional_hold_form.docx (please sign), capacity_snapshot_20261204.csv (internal node-level snapshot)

Summary of what we can do now:
- Redwood will place a 30-day soft hold covering a 120 A100-equivalent allocation using a blended mix: 80 dedicated GPUs + 40 convertible ephemeral.
- If Polaris accepts quantized execution profiles (recommended), we can meet effective throughput with room for a +30% uplift in the first 60 days.
- Firm commit required by 2027-01-04 to convert ephemeral nodes into dedicated capacity. If we do not receive a firmization, ephemeral nodes may be released per our capacity policy.

Please have procurement sign and return the provisional_hold_form via the DocuSign link below. Once we receive it, I'll coordinate a 48h staging window for canary testing and share runbooks for model packaging.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/secure/document/XYZ123
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Open question for you: do you want the staging canary to be connected to your telemetry (preferred) or isolated in a sandbox for dry runs? Both are straightforward; telemetry-connected runs let us tune real token costs before firmization.

Thanks —
Chloe
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Gavin Suri <gavin.suri@polarisml.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@polarisml.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PolarisML - capacity query and provisional hold request

Chloe — thanks, that all sounds good. Procurement will sign the provisional hold form today and route the DocuSign. We prefer telemetry-connected canary tests so we can validate real token cost and throughput; please schedule the 48h window as soon as the hold is in place.

One small ask: can we provision an additional 16 GPUs as buffer (to cover an internal burst we expect in week 3)? If the soft hold can include that buffer, we'll aim to firmize for the full amount; otherwise we accept the blended plan and will request an early conversion for additional capacity if necessary.

Gavin
Gavin Suri
Head of Infrastructure, PolarisML
